display.purpose: Today's day number only. 62% width. Smaller cousins: the shopping-list remaining count (clamp(72px, 9vw, 112px), ink), Semana day numbers (56px, 44px on phones), list tally and lists-index counts (48px), next-day numbers (44px).

headline.purpose: The dish name is the interface. 70% width, max 18ch, no frame. In rows (Semana meals, lists index) the dish is 900 at 72% width, 22px to 28px. Condensed headings open word spacing to 0.08em.

title.purpose: Heads under the 6px black rule, uppercase in side blocks, 80% width.

body.purpose: Running text and UI at normal width. Readiness and ledes are 17px.

label.purpose: Weekday and month in the day column, uppercase, 75% width. Weekday never wraps, clamp(14px, 1.4vw, 17px); month clamp(14px, 1.4vw, 20px), never larger than the weekday. The small label (13px/800, 0.06em, ink-dim) serves slot labels, Semana weekdays, item-group and table heads.

narrative.overview:
DomiOS is printed like a Portuguese tear-off wall calendar crossed with the Borda d'Água almanac. White newsprint ground, black ink, almanac yellow framing the app, calendar red for the day itself. A household lives by days, so the app is built around the day as a sheet: a huge condensed red number in a fixed column, a thick black rule across the top, and what gets eaten that day set large and unframed beside it. Below today's sheet you can see the edges of the next ones.

It is dense the way a printed almanac is dense: hierarchy comes from type width and weight and from black rules, never from boxes. There are no card frames, no panel shadows and no dashboard of equal tiles. Sections start under a 6px black rule and their rows are split by hairlines. Colour has a job or it isn't there: red means today, Sunday or "running out", the single green means "tens tudo", and yellow means the shell.

Scope of this world (honest state, 2026-11-09, second pass). The first pass rebuilt the world tokens, the app shell (desktop rail, phone tab bar, "Mais" sheet, guest header) and the Hoje page. The second pass rebuilt the other three everyday destinations, Semana, Despensa and Compras (the list and the lists index), and restyled the shared components every route uses: panels lost their frames and gained the 6px rule, pills and tags went to 3px, tables and the pantry list are headed by a 2px rule, notices became a paper-shade wash, and the page fade-in is gone. Receitas, Cozinhar, Ementas, Nutrição, Preços/Produtos, Promoções, Casa, Conta and the auth pages have only been touched by that shared restyle. Their own layouts (cards, verdict chips, shelf labels, aisle hues from src/shared/tokens.css) are legacy, pending migration, not examples of this world. The store comparison in Compras still uses the legacy shelf labels and verdict bands, and the shopping list's item-group headings still carry aisle-hue dots. The public site (site/) and the admin (admin/) still use the old shared tokens and Schibsted Grotesk and are not in this world yet.
keyCharacteristics: Today's sheet is the signature: a red condensed day number in a fixed left column, a 6px black rule on top, and the dish name as the interface.
Archivo Variable runs on its width axis: condensed and heavy for numerals, dish names and headings, normal width for UI text.
Thick black rules head sections. Hairlines separate rows. No card chrome, no shadows.
Urgency is shown by dot diameter on a fixed four-step scale, not by more colours.
Almanac yellow owns the frame (rail, tab bar, Mais sheet) and the price tag. Content sits on white paper.
One motion moment: the previous day's sheet tears upward once when the day changes.

rules.name: The Calendar Red Rule
rules.body: Red marks today, Sundays and what is running out. Use it for nothing else, and never as decoration or section colour.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one green and it means "tens tudo". Prices, savings and "cheapest store" are not green. They go on the yellow price tag, including the cheapest price on each shopping-list line.

rules.name: The Yellow Frame Rule
rules.body: Almanac yellow belongs to the shell and the price tag. Don't use it as a content background or a status colour.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from width and weight on one family. Numerals and dish names are condensed (62–72%). Navigation and body copy stay at normal width, apart from the main rail destinations at 88%.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading. Labels sit inline, like the meal slot before the dish, or beside the content, like the weekday in the day column.

rules.name: The Fixed Column Rule
rules.body: Days are rows ordered by time. A day's number always sits in its own column at a fixed width, like a split-flap board.

rules.name: The Sheet Edge Rule
rules.body: To show that something is stacked or comes next, draw sheet edges (thin parallel rules). Don't use drop shadows.

dos: Do head every section with a 6px black rule and split its rows with hairlines.
Do set day numbers and counts in Archivo at 900 weight and 62% width, and dish names at 70%.
Do keep a day's number in a fixed column wherever days are listed.
Do show urgency by dot diameter on the fixed 6 / 10 / 15 / 20px scale.
Do put prices on the yellow price tag.
Do keep almanac yellow on the shell: rail, tab bar, Mais sheet, guest header.
Do open a page with the title on the left and its primary action on the right.
donts: Don't wrap content in cards, panels with chrome, or drop shadows.
Don't use calendar red for anything except today, Sundays and "running out".
Don't use green for anything except "tens tudo", including prices and savings.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't animate ordinary page mounts. The tear is the only entrance, and it happens once per day.
Don't treat the legacy route components or the aisle hues in src/shared/tokens.css as part of this world.
